title: VPC-edge-balancer Terraform module: safe upgrades, cert rotation, and layered health checks
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Goal: Converge on a single Terraform module that orchestrates internal VPC load balancing for Redwood Private: NLB fronting for TCP/KPIs, ALB for HTTP/TLS termination, and a safe upgrade/rotation workflow that guarantees no customer traffic loss and predictable failover behavior. Scope includes module API (vars/outputs), blue/green or canary-friendly Terraform apply patterns, certificate rotation hooks (customer-provided ACM/KMS-backed certs), multi-layer health checks (LB-level + application / readiness endpoints), and automated validation tests run in CI.
technical_notes: Module should expose: vpc_id, subnets, service_targets (asg/ep), listener_configs (nlb_tcp_ports, alb_http_ports), certificate_arn (optional), cert_rotation_policy (manual|auto|graceful), health_check_config (interval, timeout, healthy_threshold, path), and tags.

Upgrade strategy: implement staged apply via feature flag + canary (terraform workspace / target trick for initial canary ASG), with connection draining and session table sync. Provide 'drain_timeout' and 'check_quiesce' variables. Document steps to perform a full module replacement with zero downtime using traffic shifting rules on ALB and standby target groups.

Certificate rotation: support both ACM and customer-uploaded certs (KMS-encrypted S3). Rotation flow must: create new target listener, validate cert via staged ALB listener attachment, switch traffic, then destroy old cert. Include an optional 'cert_validation_endpoint' to proactively validate TLS handshake after rotation.

Health checks: three layers: (1) NLB TCP-level probe for basic connectivity, (2) ALB HTTP readiness probe hitting /healthz?level=ready with JSON response, (3) app-level canary transaction endpoint invoked by CI smoke test. Health check tolerances should be configurable per environment.

Observability: emit metrics tags on target group and listener ARNs; integrate with Console telemetry via redwood-proxy metrics exporter. Add CloudWatch dashboards & synthetic canary job that runs post-apply for 30 minutes.

Testing: include terratest suite that runs in ephemeral VPC with minimal instances; CI job should apply module to a sandbox account and run smoke tests including TLS handshake, header passthrough, rate-limited burst tests, and simulated instance replacement to validate draining.
Security: ensure least-privilege IAM policies for module (route53, elb:*, acm:*, kms:Decrypt for customer artifacts). Mark security_review_required and attach threat model doc link below.

Backward compatibility: module must accept legacy inputs from existing stacks; provide migration guide for older stacks that used separate NLB/ALB resources. Avoid breaking terraform state changes by offering a 'compat_mode' toggle that preserves old resource names during migration.

Rollback: automatic rollback not feasible in Terraform; instead provide a documented playbook: run 'terraform apply' with previous workspace state, validate canary endpoints, and execute DNS TTL rollback. Add a post-failure hook that re-attaches previous ALB listener if health checks fail after switch.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes a stable API and is consumed by at least one sandbox stack in CI
Canary workflow demonstrates 0% 5xx errors during a staged module upgrade in sandbox
Certificate rotation tested end-to-end with both ACM and KMS-protected cert artifacts and validated TLS handshake success
Terratest suite passes with simulated instance replacements verifying connection draining and target deregistration
CloudWatch dashboards created and a synthetic canary job alerts on failure; integration with Console telemetry validated
Migration guide written with step-by-step commands and downtime estimation for existing stacks
